outcome_evidence: Server start: `yarn dev` log shows '▲ Next.js 15.5.27', '- Local: http://localhost:3000', '✓ Ready in 3.7s' (exit 0)
Root route fresh start: `curl -s -o /tmp/root.html -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:3000/` -> HTTP 200, 708999 bytes, contains '<title>Klimadashboard Münster</title>'
Error payload/log: 'Module not found: Can't resolve \'@/assets/data/wachstum-recent.csv\'' at components/Tiles/Climate/Wachstum/WachstumChart.tsx:11

Credential cause reproduced: POST to regionalstatistik.de genesisws tablefile without auth -> HTTP 401 body {"Code":15,"Content":"Sie sind nicht berechtigt diesen Service aufzurufen..."}; env has no REGIONALSTATISTIK_* vars
assessment_summary: I inspected /workspace (commit ffb429f) and confirmed the documented method (yarn install + yarn dev) was used. The toolchain is present (node v20.18.0, npm 10.8.2, yarn 1.22.22) and dependencies are installed (609 packages, 810M, Next 15.5.27). `yarn dev` starts successfully ('✓ Ready in 3.7s', serving http://localhost:3000). However, runtime validation shows the software is not operational: a fresh `GET /` returns HTTP 200 with the correct title and tiles, but all four core category routes (/klima, /energie, /mobilitaet, /gebaeude) return HTTP 500, as do static pages (/impressum, /datenschutz, /feedback, /sammlung). The dev-server log and page error payloads pin the failure to `Module not found: Can't resolve '@/assets/data/wachstum-recent.csv'` (imported by WachstumChart.tsx). I confirmed the missing data files (wachstum-recent.csv, bip-recent.csv, einwohner.csv) and established the cause: their fetch scripts call the Regionalstatistik Genesis API which requires REGIONALSTATISTIK_USER/SECRET credentials (injected only as Docker build secrets in the project's Dockerfile). Reproducing the request without credentials yields HTTP 401. I also observed that the homepage, though working on a clean compile, degrades to HTTP 500 after any request to a broken route. Because the supplied guide does not provide these credentials and the resulting installation cannot serve its core pages, the installation is not complete/operational. Limitations: restoring credentials/data is outside validation boundaries, so I could not observe correct rendering with data present; a possible secondary filename mismatch for the bus-passenger CSV could not be conclusively established due to non-ASCII escaping in terminal output. I stopped the validation server and made no changes to the installation.
